card.name: Bomba
card.tagline: Puerto Rico — the only dance where the drummer follows the dancer. Slaves' rebellion encoded as art.
card.profile: Bomba is an umbrella term that refers to a variety of musical styles and associated dances originating in Puerto Rico. It was developed during the 17th century by enslaved Africans and their descendants on sugar plantations along coastal towns, most notably Loiza, Mayagüez, Ponce, and San Juan. It is the island's oldest musical tradition. Bomba reflects a syncretism of Puerto Rico’s many cultural groups.
card.insight: The first documentation of bomba dates to 1797, when botanist André Pierre Ledru described his impressions of inhabitants dancing and singing popular bombas in Voyage aux îles de Ténériffe, la Trinité, Saint-Thomas, Sainte-Croix et Porto Ricco. In 1998, Son del Batey was founded in San Juan, Puerto Rico, by a group of college students at the University of Puerto Rico in Mayagüez.

steps.name: Marullo
steps.description: A two step where you swing your hips and move your arms creating waves with your skirt.

steps.name: Abanico doble
steps.description: Quick step shuffling feet with back heel pushing forward.

steps.name: El Cierre
steps.description: Punctuation step used to close your dance.

steps.name: La Cuatro
steps.description: Simple version keeping hands on your hips.

steps.name: Carrera para atrás
steps.description: Moving your feet fast just like a football player with hand movements.

steps.name: Látigo
steps.description: Moving your hand like a whip.
